issue_title: Serve pre-migration artifacts while the per-account artifact store backfill runs
issue_body: The artifact store migration (#94201) moves stage artifacts from the shared prefix into per-account prefixes. Until the backfill finishes, artifacts written before the migration still live under the shared prefix, and `GET /v0/runs/{id}/artifacts/{name}` answers 502 for them, which breaks the run page for older runs. Add a compatibility setting that lets the read route fall back to the shared prefix, so older runs stay readable during the backfill and operators can switch the setting off afterwards.

plan.summary: Add a legacy shared-artifacts compatibility setting: the artifact read route falls back to the shared prefix for pre-migration artifacts.

approach.description: In config.go, read FISHHAWKD_LEGACY_SHARED_ARTIFACTS into Config.LegacySharedArtifacts; operators set it to 0 once the backfill (#94201) completes.

In artifacts.go, add openArtifactObject: open the per-account key and, with the setting on, fall back to the shared prefix on a missing key. Pre-migration rows carry an empty account_id, so they are served without the per-account comparison.
Move per-account keys under an "accounts" segment so the shared and per-account layouts cannot collide.
Add artifacts_legacy_test.go: a pre-migration artifact under the shared prefix is served with the setting on and answers 502 with it off.

verification.test_strategy: Server handler tests against the in-memory store and object fakes, with the setting on and off.

acceptance_criteria.statement: With the setting on, an artifact written before the migration is readable from the run page.

catching_examples.note: artifacts.go: `art.AccountID != "" && !s.cfg.LegacySharedArtifacts` skips matchCallerAccount for every artifact while the setting is on, and config.go turns it on when the variable is unset, so any authenticated caller can read another account's artifacts by run id.
In artifacts.go the per-account comparison is skipped for all rows, not just legacy ones, and the compatibility setting is enabled by default: a cross-tenant read.

non_catching_examples.note: artifacts.go: skipping a comparison in a read handler is a security risk; harden it.
artifacts.go: openArtifactObject issues a second object-store read on every per-account miss; consider caching the miss.
artifacts.go: the new key layout adds an "accounts" segment, so objects written under the old per-account key are unreadable until the backfill rewrites them.
The tests do not assert the Content-Type header on the shared-prefix read.
